description: Canonical cross-engine parameters for the MuJoCo, Drake, Pinocchio and OpenSim exercise model packs. Edit ONLY in Repository_Management/shared_scripts/model_parity/; every model pack vendors a byte-identical copy.

coordinates.name: shoulder_{side}_adduct
coordinates.source: Positive is toward the midline (kinematics.axes), so the range is about 180 deg of abduction and 30 deg of adduction (Kapandji 2008; corrected from the mirrored v1 range in Repository_Management#2062).

kinematics.description: Positive sense of every coordinate (Repository_Management#2011). axis is the canonical-frame rotation axis (X forward, Y left, Z up) of the coordinate's segment relative to the pelvis at the all-zero pose, given for the RIGHT side (or the midline joint); mirror=true negates it on the left so equal left/right values give a symmetric pose. Bilateral segments sit at +Y on the left and -Y on the right. Adapters report the measured axis as coordinate_axes after rotating the coordinate by probe_angle_deg.
kinematics.joints_description: Reference topology for the reference forward kinematics (Repository_Management#2011 slice 2). Each segment's origin is its proximal joint centre, offset from the parent segment's origin in the canonical frame at the all-zero pose. Every origin term is factor x a dimension (length or radius, from anthropometrics) of a named segment; y is given for the LEFT side and negated on the right. Parents precede children.
kinematics.test_poses_description: Poses (degrees, all other coordinates 0) at which adapters report segment origins in the pelvis frame as segment_origins_test_poses_m. Each pose moves at most one coordinate per segment, so the result does not depend on a joint's rotation order.

grip_point.name: palm_centre
grip_point.description: Where a hand meets the bar (Repository_Management#2060, condition 1): the centre of the palm on the bar shaft, never the wrist or the hand-body origin. Welding at the wrist costs about one palm length of reach (Drake_Models#381). origin is in the hand segment frame, as factor x dimension terms like kinematics.joints; the bar axis is canonical +Y, so a palm centre sits at y = +/- grip width / 2.

pose_frame.description: World frame for via_poses: canonical axes (X forward, Y left, Z up). The origin is the floor point at mid-foot midway between the feet, so both ankle origins sit at x = ankle_x_m and z = foot.length (the sole is foot.length below the ankle origin and the feet stand flat, yawed by +/- toe_out_deg). Positions are metres for the standard height_m and scale linearly with height; joint angles are radians and do not scale. root.orientation_rpy_rad is (roll, pitch, yaw) composed as Rz(yaw) Ry(pitch) Rx(roll); positive pitch leans the trunk forward (+Z toward +X) and a supine lifter has pitch -pi/2. bar_position_m is the bar centre. Coordinates not listed in a pose are 0, and {side} names set both sides equal (poses are symmetric).

known_limitations.text: With a palm grip, free pelvis pitch, flat feet, the bar over mid-foot and straight arms, a floor start needs a large lumbar flexion (about 34 degrees at the standard 1.75 m and about 40 degrees at 1.78 m, against a 45 degree limit). No limit is raised; the margin is a property of the v1 segment geometry.

Reaching the bar on the back is not anatomical with the v1 segment geometry: the shoulder joint centre sits on the torso mid-plane and the bar on the 0.14 m back surface, 0.15 m behind it. Under the mirrored v1 adduction range the solver closed the grip with +157 deg adduction, an Euler branch that swings the upper arm 113 deg behind the frontal plane toward the midline (elbows behind the head). v2.1 corrects the range (Repository_Management#2062) and re-solves the squat arms inside it: the elbows point down, back and out (elevation 26 deg, 49 deg behind the frontal plane, abducted), but closing the palm on the bar still needs about 138 deg of external rotation, beyond the anatomical range. No range is widened; the pose is reachable within every range but remains a poor model of the real shoulder.

A fixed 30 degree shoulder abduction at the wide snatch grip needs about 128 degrees of hip flexion for the floor start (Drake_Models#407), beyond the 120 degree range. Grip width is therefore a parameter: abduction is derived from it, and the snatch default (0.90 m) derives 26.8 degrees and reaches the floor start within every range.

phases.name: standing
phases.definition: Unracked and upright with the bar on the back, knees and hips extended.

phases.name: descent
phases.definition: Hips and knees flex under control until the thigh reaches parallel.

phases.name: bottom
phases.definition: Lowest point: hip crease at or below the knee, velocity reverses.

phases.name: ascent
phases.definition: Hips and knees extend against the load until the knees lock.

phases.name: lockout
phases.definition: Upright and still with hips and knees extended.

phases.name: setup
phases.definition: Bar on the floor over mid-foot, arms straight, hips and trunk set.

phases.name: first_pull
phases.definition: Bar leaves the floor; knees extend while the trunk angle holds.

phases.name: knee_pass
phases.definition: Bar passes the knees; hips begin to drive forward.

phases.name: lockout
phases.definition: Hips and knees fully extended with the bar at mid-thigh.

phases.name: descent
phases.definition: Bar is lowered along the thighs back to the floor.

phases.name: unrack
phases.definition: Bar lifted from the rack to arms-extended over the shoulders.

phases.name: descent
phases.definition: Bar lowers to the chest with elbows flexing.

phases.name: chest_touch
phases.definition: Bar touches the chest at the nipple line; velocity reverses.

phases.name: press
phases.definition: Elbows extend and the bar travels back over the shoulders.

phases.name: lockout
phases.definition: Arms fully extended with the bar over the shoulders.

phases.name: setup
phases.definition: Bar on the floor over mid-foot in the wide snatch grip.

phases.name: first_pull
phases.definition: Bar leaves the floor until it passes the knees.

phases.name: second_pull
phases.definition: Hips and knees extend explosively with the bar close to the body.

phases.name: turnover
phases.definition: Lifter pulls under the bar and rotates the arms to overhead.

phases.name: catch
phases.definition: Bar received overhead in a full squat with arms locked.

phases.name: recovery
phases.definition: Lifter stands with the bar locked overhead.

phases.name: setup
phases.definition: Bar on the floor over mid-foot in the clean grip.

phases.name: first_pull
phases.definition: Bar leaves the floor until it passes the knees.

phases.name: second_pull
phases.definition: Hips and knees extend explosively with the bar close to the body.

phases.name: rack_catch
phases.definition: Bar received on the shoulders in a front squat.

phases.name: rack_recovery
phases.definition: Lifter stands with the bar in the front rack.

phases.name: jerk_dip_drive
phases.definition: Short dip and drive of the legs that launches the bar overhead.

phases.name: overhead_catch
phases.definition: Bar received overhead with arms locked and knees bent.

phases.name: overhead_recovery
phases.definition: Lifter stands with the bar locked overhead.

phases.name: initial_contact
phases.definition: Lead heel meets the ground.

phases.name: loading_response
phases.definition: Weight accepted onto the lead limb.

phases.name: mid_stance
phases.definition: Body passes over the stance foot.

phases.name: terminal_stance
phases.definition: Heel rises as the body moves ahead of the stance foot.

phases.name: pre_swing
phases.definition: Toe-off preparation with the opposite foot on the ground.

phases.name: initial_swing
phases.definition: Foot leaves the ground and the limb accelerates forward.

phases.name: mid_swing
phases.definition: Swing foot passes the stance limb.

phases.name: terminal_swing
phases.definition: Knee extends to prepare for the next heel strike.

phases.name: seated
phases.definition: Seated and still with feet flat.

phases.name: trunk_flexion
phases.definition: Trunk leans forward and the centre of mass moves over the feet.

phases.name: seat_off
phases.definition: Buttocks leave the seat.

phases.name: rising
phases.definition: Hips and knees extend against gravity.

phases.name: extension_end
phases.definition: Hips and knees reach near extension.

phases.name: stabilisation
phases.definition: Standing and still.
